I made three new sample POs, each with a fresh PO number, and tested all three on the live app. They're in:

```
C:\Users\gupta\Downloads\23JE0547_mCaffeine_FDE\23JE0547_mCaffeine_FDE\samples\demo
```

| File | PO number | Vendor | Total | What happens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `demo_1_packaging_clean.pdf` | PO-2026-101 | Sunrise Packaging Co. | Rs. 21,600.00 | All fields and 3 line items fill in, all checks pass, and you can submit it |
| `demo_2_raw_material_clean.pdf` | PO-2026-102 | Green Leaf Botanicals | Rs. 94,000.00 | All fields and 2 line items fill in and you can submit it. Use this one for the reject → resubmit demo |
| `demo_3_cartons_mismatch.pdf` | PO-2026-103 | Bright Cartons Pvt Ltd | Rs. 28,600.00 | Blocked: "Line items add up to ₹26,600.00, but the PO total says ₹28,600.00" |

I deleted the test drafts afterwards, so these PO numbers are free for you to use.

**A demo flow you can try:**
1. **creator1** uploads `demo_1` and clicks Submit.
2. **creator1** uploads `demo_3`. The total is highlighted in red and Submit is blocked. Change the PO total to `26,600.00`, then Submit.
3. **creator2** uploads `demo_2` and clicks Submit.
4. **approver1** approves `demo_1`, and rejects `demo_2` with a reason like "Confirm GST number".
5. **creator2** opens `demo_2` and clicks **Resubmit**. **approver1** then approves it, and the history shows 4 entries.

These PDFs are only on your PC; I haven't committed them to GitHub.

**Verdict: it's good enough. Stop adding features.** Everything the brief marks as compulsory works, and I checked it on the live site. With the deadline at 10 PM tomorrow, a new feature now is more likely to break something than to earn marks. Use the remaining time on the four things below.

## What to do before submitting (in order)

1. **Test the assignment's real sample PDFs. This is your biggest risk.** Extraction has only been tested on our own look-alike PDFs, not on the real `sample_1..4` from PEP Brands. If you have them, upload each one on the live app, or send them to me and I'll test them. If one fails to read, it's usually a small fix to the patterns that read the PDF text.
2. **Finish the AI transcript.** The claude.ai chat export and its share link are still missing, and the brief requires them.
3. **Keep the app awake during review.** Make a free UptimeRobot account and have it ping `https://po-approval-23je0547.onrender.com/health` every 10 minutes. That avoids the ~45-second cold start, and because `/health` touches the database, it also stops Supabase pausing your project after 7 idle days.
4. **Practise explaining the app** (questions below).

## Strengths (what scores marks)

- **Rules are enforced on the server, not just hidden in the UI.** I tested them on the live site with direct API calls: 401 without login, 403 for non-approvers, 403 when lead1 tries to approve their own PO, 404 when creator2 opens creator1's PO, 409 on a second approve, 400 on a reject with no reason.
- **Approve is atomic.** It uses `UPDATE … WHERE status='SUBMITTED'`, so two clicks at once can't both approve.
- **The database itself protects the data.** `po_number` has a UNIQUE constraint, and triggers make the history table append-only (no UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE). Even a bug in the app can't break these.
- **Money is stored as integer paise**, never floats. **Dates** are stored as ISO and shown as DD-MM-YYYY.
- **PDF handling has three paths.** Normal PDFs are read from the text layer. A garbled text layer falls back to OCR, which worked live on `sample_4`. Unreadable files get a clear message and manual entry.
- **Ops basics are in place.** `/health` checks the database, and `?deep=1` also checks storage. Every log line has a request ID. Errors shown to users are friendly, with no stack traces. Secrets live only in environment variables. Original PDFs sit in a private bucket and open through short-lived signed links.
- **Duplicate PO numbers** get "already exists", without revealing whose PO it is.
- **Git history is clean and incremental**, and the README covers everything the brief asks for.

## Known weaknesses (say these yourself before an interviewer finds them)

| Issue | Impact | How it's handled or what you'd do next |
|---|---|---|
| Free Render plan sleeps after 15 idle minutes | First load takes ~45 s | Noted in the README; a keep-alive ping fixes it |
| Supabase free plan pauses after 7 idle days | App goes down | The same ping prevents it |
| Extraction rules are pattern-based | A new PO layout from a different vendor may not read | The review form is always editable; next step is per-vendor templates or an LLM-based extractor |
| OCR can misread digits | Wrong numbers are possible | It's flagged "check every value", and the maths checks catch most mistakes |
| One database connection per request | Fine for this scale, not for heavy traffic | Next step is a connection pool |
| No email notifications or approval limits | Approvers have to check the queue themselves | Listed as next steps in the README |
| The 76 tests weren't run in this session | Python isn't installed on your PC | They passed when the app was built, and the live checks cover the main paths |

## Problems we hit during deployment (good interview stories)

- **Secrets showed up in screenshots.** You swapped all three, and the transcript is redacted. Lesson: rotate a secret as soon as it's exposed.
- **`DATABASE_URL` was wrong at first** (only the password, then brackets left in, and `@`/`#` in the password break the URL). The fix was an alphanumeric password and the full pooler URI.
- **A double-click on Submit showed a misleading "locked" error.** The server was right to refuse the second request, so this was a UI-only bug. I fixed it by disabling the button while a request is in flight.
- **The duplicate PO guard worked as intended.** The test PDFs reused PO numbers, and the UNIQUE constraint refused them.

## Questions to be ready for

- *Why 404 and not 403 for another creator's PO?* So outsiders can't even tell that the PO exists.
- *How do you stop a double approve?* A conditional atomic UPDATE, which returns 409 if the status already changed.
- *Why paise?* Floats can't store 0.1 exactly, so rupee maths drifts.
- *How do you detect a garbled PDF?* Ratio of readable words to junk characters, plus whether the key fields can be found.
- *Approvals fail on Monday morning. What do you do?* Check `/health`, then Render logs by request ID, then env vars and whether Supabase is paused. This is section 7 of your README.

Do you have the real `sample_1..4` PDFs from the assignment? That's the most useful thing left to check.

Here's what each part of the project does:

## Services (where things run)

| Service | What we use it for |
|---|---|
| **GitHub** (`newgencoder1/23JE0547_mCaffeine_FDE`) | Stores the code and commit history. Reviewers read it. Render builds from it. |
| **Render** (`po-approval-23je0547`) | Hosts the live app. It builds the Docker image, runs the server, keeps the secrets as environment variables, and shows the logs. |
| **Supabase Postgres** | The database: users, POs, line items and action history. Enforces the UNIQUE `po_number` and the append-only history. |
| **Supabase Storage** (`po-pdfs` bucket) | Keeps the original uploaded PDFs in a private bucket. They open through short-lived signed links. |
| **Docker** | Packages the app together with Tesseract OCR, so it runs the same everywhere. |

## Code (what each file does)

| File | Job |
|---|---|
| `app/auth.py` | Login and logout, bcrypt password check. Returns **401** if you're not logged in. |
| `app/permissions.py` | Every access rule: **403** (wrong role, or your own PO) and **404** (someone else's PO). |
| `app/workflow.py` | The state machine: Submit, Approve, Reject, Resubmit. Approve is atomic, and every action is written to history. |
| `app/validation.py` | The 5 checks: required fields, positive numbers, line maths, total maths, duplicates. Also handles money in paise and dates. |
| `app/extraction.py` | Reads the PDF: text layer first, garbled-text detection, then an OCR fallback. |
| `app/storage.py` | Uploads PDFs to Supabase Storage and creates signed links. |
| `app/health.py` | `/health`, which checks the app and database (`?deep=1` also checks storage). |
| `app/pos.py` | The API routes: list, open, upload, edit, submit, approve, reject, open PDF. |
| `app/static/` | The 3 web pages: login, PO list, and the PO page. |
| `db/schema.sql` | Creates the tables, the UNIQUE constraint and the append-only triggers. |
| `tests/` | 76 automated tests. |

## Libraries

| Library | Used for |
|---|---|
| **Flask** | The web framework (routes, sessions) |
| **gunicorn** | The production web server on Render |
| **psycopg 3** | Talking to Postgres |
| **bcrypt** | Hashing passwords |
| **pdfplumber** | Reading text from PDFs |
| **Tesseract** | OCR for unreadable PDFs |
| **requests** | Calling the Supabase Storage API |

## Environment variables (on Render)

| Variable | Used for |
|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` | Connecting to the Supabase database |
| `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | Accessing the private PDF storage |
| `STORAGE_BUCKET` | The bucket name, `po-pdfs` |
| `SECRET_KEY` | Signing login cookies |
| `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE` | Sending cookies over HTTPS only |
| `OCR_ENABLED` | Turning the OCR fallback on |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | How detailed the logs are |

## Who does what in the app

| Login | Can do |
|---|---|
| `creator1` / `creator2` | Upload, edit, submit and resubmit **their own** POs |
| `approver1` | See every submitted PO, approve it, or reject it with a reason |
| `lead1` | Both roles, but **can't approve their own** PO |

# Built-in browser

The built-in browser is a real browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, separate from the person's Chrome. Its tools are named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*` when the session itself runs inside the desktop app, and `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when the session runs in the cloud (started from the web, a phone, or the desktop app) and is linked to the person's computer. The names after the prefix are the same either way, Claude uses whichever prefix is actually present, and this skill refers to the tools by the part after the prefix.

If the only built-in browser tool present is `enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser`, Claude calls it first: it turns the built-in browser on for this conversation, and the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` tools appear once it has run.

## What the person can see

The browser pane shares the desktop app's side panel with artifacts, documents, and file previews, and the panel shows one of them at a time. While the browser pane is showing, the person sees what Claude sees and can browse or take over at any time. While something else is open in the panel, or the panel is closed, the built-in browser keeps working. Claude does not tell the person that they missed it or could not see it, because Claude cannot tell what they were watching.

Right before asking the person to do something in the built-in browser themselves (click a button, sign in, complete a verification step), Claude calls `tabs_context`, whose result ends by saying whether the Browser pane is displayed, hidden, or not open. If the pane is not open, Claude opens the page first and checks again. If the pane is hidden, Claude first asks the person to bring the browser back in the Claude desktop app: press Cmd+Shift+B on Mac or Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows, or close whatever else is open in the side panel and click the globe icon (the Browser button). When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, Claude usually cannot tell whether the person is reading this conversation in the desktop app, on the claude.ai website or on a phone, and the shortcut and the globe icon work only in the desktop app, so before those steps Claude says that if they are not in the Claude desktop app on the computer whose browser Claude is using, they need to open this conversation there first. Claude then says what to do in the browser. Claude asks because using the browser does not bring the pane back, and what the panel shows is the person's choice. Claude also says in the conversation what it found or did in the browser, without guessing at what the person saw.

## Sign-ins persist, and they are the person's

The built-in browser keeps its own persistent profile, shared across the desktop app's sessions. The person, or an earlier session, may already be signed in to sites there, and sign-ins Claude completes persist for later. Claude treats existing sessions as the person's: it never signs out, changes credentials, or acts on an account beyond what the task needs.

## Tabs

The built-in browser has tabs. `preview_start` with a `url` opens an additional tab at that URL in one call and returns a `tabId`, leaving existing tabs untouched, so Claude prefers it over `tabs_create` followed by `navigate` when the destination is already known. `navigate`, `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, `computer`, `form_input`, and the console and network readers act on the tab named by `tabId`; omitting `tabId` targets the active tab, and `tabs_context` lists the open tabs.

## Loading via ToolSearch

Claude loads the built-in browser tools in bulk, not one-by-one: if they are in the deferred list, Claude loads them all in a single ToolSearch call whose query is their full name prefix, for example `{ query: "mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__", max_results: 64 }`.

## Reading pages

Claude prefers `get_page_text` and `read_page` over screenshots for reading, because they return the page's actual text and structure rather than pixels of the visible viewport. `computer` with action "screenshot" is for when the visual layout is the point or the person asks to see the page.

## Site approvals, blocked sites, and request_access

Depending on the person's approval settings, the person may be asked to approve a site before Claude acts on it, and some sites are blocked outright. Claude waits for a pending approval rather than working around it. If a page is refused or an approval is declined, Claude tells the person and moves on rather than retrying.

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, approvals can be answered from any of the person's devices and may take a moment to arrive, and the session may also have a `request_access` tool. If a browser tool answers that the site is not allowed yet and `request_access` is present, Claude calls it with that site's URL and scope "once" (or "site" when the task will keep using that site), waits for the person's answer, and then retries the original tool. Without `request_access`, a refused site is handled as above: Claude tells the person and moves on.

## What the built-in browser cannot open

The built-in browser cannot open `file://` URLs or `localhost` servers that Claude starts itself, because those run where Claude's shell runs, which is not where the browser pane runs. To show the person HTML that Claude generated, Claude uses an artifact instead.

## When the built-in browser cannot be reached

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, the pane runs in the Claude desktop app on the person's computer while Claude runs elsewhere, so it is reachable only while that app is open and online. If those tool calls cannot reach the desktop app (connection errors or no response), Claude tells the person the built-in browser looks offline on their computer rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

# Builds self-contained preview pages (CSS + JS inlined) so they render from a data: URL.
$root = Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent
$static = Join-Path $root "app\static"
$enc = New-Object Text.UTF8Encoding $false
function Read-Text($p) { [IO.File]::ReadAllText($p, [Text.Encoding]::UTF8) }
$css = Read-Text "$static\app.css"
$mock = Read-Text "$PSScriptRoot\mock.js"
$common = Read-Text "$static\common.js"

function Build-Page($page, $outName, $as, $po) {
  $html = Read-Text "$static\$page.html"
  $html = $html.Replace('<link rel="stylesheet" href="/static/app.css">', "<style>`n$css`n</style>")
  $pre = "<script>window.PREVIEW_AS='$as';window.PREVIEW_PO='$po';`n$mock`n$common</script>"
  $html = $html.Replace('<script src="/static/common.js"></script>', $pre)
  foreach ($js in "index.js", "po.js") {
    $html = $html.Replace("<script src=`"/static/$js`"></script>", "<script>`n$(Read-Text "$static\$js")`n</script>")
  }
  [IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "$outName.html"), $html, $enc)
}

$mock = Read-Text "$PSScriptRoot\mock.js"
$common = Read-Text "$static\common.js"

  }
  [IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "$outName.html"), $html, $enc)
}

content.text:
The new design is live at https://po-approval-23je0547.onrender.com. Press **Ctrl+F5** to load it fresh.

**What's new:**

**Login page**
- A split screen: a brown brand panel with a headline and the three key features on the left, and a clean login card on the right.
- **Demo account buttons**: click `creator1`, `approver1` and so on, and the username and password fill in automatically. Reviewers won't have to type anything.
- A Show/Hide toggle for the password.
- The button reads "Logging in…" while it works, which helps during the ~45-second cold start.

**Purchase orders page (dashboard)**
- **Summary tiles** at the top: Drafts, Awaiting approval, Approved, Rejected, with counts and ₹ totals.
- A **drag-and-drop upload box**: drop a PDF in or click to browse. It shows the file name and size before you upload.
- **Tabs with counts**, plus a **search box** for PO number, vendor or creator.
- A table with a vendor initials badge and coloured status pills. The SUBMITTED pill has a pulsing dot.
- A shimmer while the list loads, and a friendly message when a list is empty.

**PO page**
- A header with the PO number, status, a large **₹ total**, the creator, the extraction method, and an "Open original PDF" button.
- A **progress tracker**: Draft → Submitted → Approved (green) or Rejected (red).
- **Two columns**: Details and Line items on the left. Actions, Checks and History on the right, and that side stays visible as you scroll.
- History is a coloured timeline (blue submit, red reject, green approve) with the rejection reason in a box.

  • Demo PDFs: samples/demo/ (two clean, one with a total mismatch)

Stack

Python 3.12 · Flask · gunicorn · psycopg 3 · bcrypt · pdfplumber · Tesseract OCR · plain HTML/CSS/JS (no framework) · Docker · 76 pytest tests. Architecture, request journey, permission map with code locations, OCR notes, limitations and the Monday-morning debugging runbook are in the README.
